name: MediaDash
description: Whole-library housekeeping for Jellyfin: finds duplicates, broken files, oversized encodes, unwanted or missing language tracks, and misplaced files — then fixes them safely. Dry-run mode and a recycle bin protect your media by default.
overview: The one plugin a Jellyfin library owner needs.

versions.changelog: Jellyfin 12.0 compatible entry (same binary as the 10.11 entry below). Jellyfin 12 is a version-scheme rename of what would have been 10.12, not a hard API break, so the same zip loads on both host lines. Verified against a running 12.0.0 server.

Settings tab: fixes width squish on wide monitors. Jellyfin's core CSS caps every form at 54em on >=50em viewports, and the Settings tab wrapper is a form, so the whole settings surface (page header, nav chips, card grid) was stuck at ~800px on a 1080p monitor. Plugin-scoped `form { max-width: none }` overrides that. Community stats opt-in is now pre-ticked in the first-run wizard and on Settings > Safety - unticking + Save opts you out and clears the install UUID, and nothing about what is/isn't sent has changed (see docs/PRIVACY.md).

Fixes v0.7.0 which shipped an incomplete zip (only the main dll, missing System.Diagnostics.PerformanceCounter.dll + 3 other dependency dlls). On Windows this made the plugin fail to load with a FileNotFoundException, showing as NotSupported in Dashboard > Plugins. v0.7.1 ships the full dependency set. Also two Settings tab polish fixes: page now uses the full window width instead of capping at 1400px, and the Scheduled fix time input is now visible against the dark card background (Chrome/Edge were rendering the clock indicator in a colour that vanished against the card).

Two features. Configurable fix schedule: Settings > Safety now has a time picker for when the daily fix run fires (default 03:00, including re-encodes) - the existing 'Only run when the server is idle' flag still vetoes runs when someone is watching, and the change takes effect without a Jellyfin restart. UI localisation: the dashboard, tab labels, settings section headings, first-run wizard, and the plugin's scheduled-task names now translate to whichever UI language the current Jellyfin user has selected. English is the source of truth; de/es/fr/it/nl/pt-BR/ru/zh-CN ship as machine-translated seeds and are unproofread - community PRs to refine any locale are welcome. Falls back cleanly (de-AT to de to en) so an unknown locale never breaks the page. Deep settings tooltips (Quality, Advanced, Libraries, Recycle bin internals) stay English for now - the framework accepts new keys without any code change, so those get wrapped as needed.

Pre-beta polish. New 'Copy diagnostics' button on the Errors tab drops a clipboard-ready markdown blob (plugin/Jellyfin/OS/runtime versions plus all recorded errors) that pastes cleanly into a GitHub issue. New 'Report an issue' link in Settings > Maintenance opens the tracker in a new tab. Wizard step 5 and the Settings 'Missing subtitles' row now show a live indicator whether a subtitle provider is installed - green with the provider name when ready, amber with 'Install one from Dashboard > Plugins > Catalog, the API key lives on that plugin's page, not here' when not - closing the discovery gap about where subtitle providers are configured (they live inside Jellyfin proper, MediaDash inherits them). Media sorter gains an optional 'Anime folder' target: items with Jellyfin's 'Anime' genre tag (case-insensitive) route there instead of Movies or TV. Leave it empty to keep existing behaviour. If your anime isn't tagged, install the AniDB scraper from Dashboard > Plugins > Catalog and Jellyfin will apply the tag automatically. CHANGELOG.md refreshed to point at GitHub Releases.

New Missing subtitles fix type: flags videos with no subtitle in any wanted language and downloads one via Jellyfin's already-configured subtitle providers (OpenSubtitles etc.) - no new API keys. First-run experience is now a multi-step wizard that walks each feature one at a time (Welcome, Libraries + access-check, Duplicates, Broken files, Oversized files, Languages incl. missing-subs mode, Media sorter, Safety net, Done), triggered only on fresh installs (survives plugin updates via FirstRunDone). Preferred-GPU picker moved into the Oversized step alongside the hardware-encoder toggle. AMD APU (Rembrandt / Phoenix - Ryzen 6000/7000 iGPUs) GPU percentage now reads from /sys/class/drm/cardN/device/gpu_metrics when gpu_busy_percent is pinned at 0, fixing the 0.0% GPU reading on affected hosts. Overview 'Space you could reclaim' total now includes issues you've already approved (Queued), not just Detected ones - matches what the Issues tab shows. PLAN.md rewritten around a whole-library housekeeping scope with explicit non-goals (no acquisition, no metadata authoring) and a prioritised roadmap for the next scanners.

History tab grows an All / Succeeded / Failed / Dry run filter row with live per-bucket counts so you can jump straight to the failed items after a big fix run instead of scrolling. Backed by a new Success column on the history table (schema v2; legacy rows back-filled). Settings tab redesign: sticky page header with a gradient Save button, restyled chip nav, 2-column grid of glass-effect cards with tinted icon boxes, Plus Jakarta Sans typography, and sections re-ordered so Maintenance actions live in their own card instead of buried in Advanced. Whole plugin surface is now centred and widened to min(1400px, 96vw) so the 2-column grid and drive-storage cards have room to breathe.

The 'Run fixes now' button used to appear to do nothing when every attempted fix failed fast (typical on a Linux server where the jellyfin user doesn't own the media files) - the progress bar just flashed and the user was left to click through Errors to find out what happened. Fix runs now finish with a dashboard alert summarising attempted / succeeded / failed and the dominant reason, with reason-specific instructions (e.g. the exact chown command to grant Jellyfin write access). Manually-approved issues under types set to 'Detect only' now actually run - previously they were silently filtered out. The Overview drive list now always shows the drive the recycle bin lives on, even when it's on a Docker overlay / tmpfs / btrfs subvolume that DriveInfo filters out, so you notice when the bin is filling your system disk. New 'Check library access' button in first-run setup that probes read+write on every library folder and reports pass/fail per folder with a plain-language reason, so ownership/ACL problems get caught before you approve anything.

Media sorter now surfaces a clear, actionable error message on the Errors tab when a target folder is misconfigured (doesn't exist, sits outside every Jellyfin library, or isn't writable by the Jellyfin user) instead of silently creating hundreds of unfixable issues. The fixer also distinguishes those cases at fix time and pre-checks free disk space for cross-volume moves. 'Empty recycle bin now' used to freeze the UI on large bins and silently fail on older ApiClient builds - it now runs in the background with a determinate progress bar, and any per-batch permission or I/O errors show as a dashboard alert instead of tanking the whole operation on the first bad file.

New 'Misplaced files' fix type: MediaDash spots a movie sitting in your TV folder (or a TV episode sitting in Movies) and moves it into the correct folder. Set the two target folders under Settings > Libraries; classification uses Jellyfin's own metadata by default with a filename-pattern fallback (SxxExx / NxN => TV). LibraryGuard refuses moves outside your Jellyfin libraries. Optional new toggle to rename files after a successful re-encode to a canonical form: 'Name (Year) - 1080p.mkv' for movies, 'Series - S03E14 - 1080p.mkv' for TV episodes. Every primary button and settings chip now shows a tooltip on hover.

Recycle bin pre-checks free space on cross-volume moves and Overview warns when the bin lives on a different volume than your libraries. Issues tab now shows queued items alongside detected ones (they no longer vanish on approval) and refreshes live during a fix run so items disappear as they succeed. New 'Retry all fixes' button on the Errors tab clears the buffer and reruns the queue.

Polish pass. File browser and fix task catch UnauthorizedAccessException with an actionable message (points at Jellyfin's user needing write access) instead of a generic 500; denied fixes also show in History. New Encode preset dropdown (Faster/Balanced/Best) for software re-encodes. Quality scanner ignores files smaller than a configurable threshold (100 MB default) and skips HDR content by default so naive transcodes don't destroy HDR metadata. Errors tab collapses repeated identical entries into a single row with a count. New live filter-by-filename search on the Issues tab.

Linux hotfix. /Status endpoint crashed on Linux because SystemStats referenced Windows-only PerformanceCounter at class-load time. Now loaded lazily so the type only resolves inside the Windows branch. Sample() also gains a top-level try/catch that surfaces future failures to the Errors tab instead of taking the tab down silently.

Multi-GPU monitoring (NVIDIA / Windows PDH / Linux sysfs, per-card) with per-GPU cells. New Preferred GPU dropdown routes re-encodes to a specific card via ffmpeg -gpu for NVENC/AMF. Windows GPU counter fix: PDH counters are cached across polls and aggregated max-across-engines so numbers match Task Manager. Overview polls every 3s while visible, and metric cells update in place so the tab no longer flickers. New Errors tab with red badge exposes swallowed plugin exceptions. Approve refreshes status so 'nothing to fix' isn't stale. Approve-all button restyled and aligned. 'Space you could reclaim' card no longer overhangs its container.

GPU monitoring now covers AMD and modern Intel iGPUs on Linux via /sys/class/drm sysfs when nvidia-smi isn't available. GPU cell shows the data source (NVIDIA / Linux sysfs). Sidebar icon changed from generic 'dashboard' to 'auto_fix_high' so MediaDash stands out at a glance.

System performance card now reports whole-host CPU and RAM (Windows via GetSystemTimes/GlobalMemoryStatusEx, Linux via /proc). macOS and containers show N/A. Drives card now lists every fixed drive on the host, with a badge on library-hosting drives.

Overview leads with a live System performance card (Jellyfin CPU%, memory, NVIDIA GPU% via nvidia-smi) at the top, then Library drive storage, then everything else. Themed to match the rest of the plugin with greenâ†’amberâ†’red bar colouring.

Overview polish. Scan/Fix buttons now cancel the running task (red Stop state) with a matching themed gradient look. Current file shown under the progress bar. Per-drive storage card. No more 3-second flicker while scanning/fixing. Fix run processes smallest files first so early completions free disk space for the big ones.

Files tab restyled to match the rest of the plugin: 14px rounded cards, Jellyfin-blue accent on headers/hover, tabular numbers for size/date, breadcrumb pill, refined bulk action bar and folder-picker modal. Visual only, no functional changes.
Files tab: multi-select with bulk delete/move/download, filter box, and a modal folder picker that replaces the raw path prompt for move/copy operations.

Files tab: sortable columns (Name, Size, Modified), directories stay on top. Up button fixed at library roots. Issues tab: click a file path to open its folder in the Files tab; new 'Approve all N issues (all types)' button when no type filter is set.
Files tab: drag-and-drop uploads. Drop one or many files onto the list to upload into the current folder. Multi-file selection via the Upload button too. Admin-only, same safety as before.

New Files tab: browse, upload, download, rename, move, copy and delete files inside your library folders. Deletes go to the recycle bin. Every operation is refused if it targets anything outside a configured library.

Fewer false-positive unplayable flags; less aggressive re-encode disk check so batches can proceed on tighter drives; live progress bar during transcodes; helpful hint when 'Run fixes now' has nothing to do; new 'Reset scan data' button in Settings > Advanced to recover from stuck state without reinstalling. Existing installs get a one-time decode-cache wipe so the playability fix takes effect immediately.
Initial public release.
